subproblem.title: Weak convergence survives translations and dilations with factors tending to 1
subproblem.statement: Let P, n, Q ∈ ℕ and μ := μH[n] on ℝ^P. Let g_k : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q (k ∈ ℕ) be locally μ-integrable, let g : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be arbitrary, let y ∈ ℝ^P, and let c_k > 0 with c_k → 1. Suppose ∫ f g_k dμ → ∫ f g dμ for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ. Then for every such f, ∫ f(x) g_k(y + c_k x) dμ(x) → ∫ f(x) g(y + x) dμ(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n Q : ℕ) (gs : ℕ → Euclid P → Euclid Q) (g : Euclid P → Euclid Q) (y : Euclid P) (mus : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ k, LocallyIntegrable (gs k) μH[(n : ℝ)]) → (∀ k, 0 < mus k) → Tendsto mus atTop (𝓝 1) → (∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, f x • gs k x ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x • g x ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]))) → ∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, f x • gs k (y + mus k • x) ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x • g (y + x) ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: facts (b) and (c) of the parent proof (step 0) and its departure [D2]. The weak limits in Simon's chapter-A.txt lines 125–133 ('ψ_{βx,1} = lim φ_{x+λ_jβx,λ_j} = ψ') need the uniform bound proved below. Write μ := μH[n] and c_k := mus k.
1. Change of variables. Let c > 0, y ∈ ℝ^P and T(x) := y + cx. Hausdorff measure is translation invariant and satisfies μH[n](cA) = c^n μH[n](A) (Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_smul₀, map_homothety_hausdorffMeasure). So μ(T⁻¹B) = μ(c⁻¹(B − y)) = c^{−n}μ(B) for Borel B, i.e. T_#μ = c^{−n}μ. Since T is a measurable embedding, ∫ h(y + cx) dμ(x) = ∫ h d(T_#μ) = c^{−n}∫ h dμ for every h : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q. If h is not integrable, then neither is h∘T, and both sides are 0.
2. Fix f continuous with spt f ⊆ B̄_R(0), R > 0. Put f_k(w) := f((w − y)/c_k) and f_∞(w) := f(w − y). Step 1 gives ∫ f(x) g_k(y + c_k x) dμ(x) = c_k^{−n} ∫ f_k g_k dμ and ∫ f(x) g(y + x) dμ(x) = ∫ f_∞ g dμ.
3. Since c_k → 1, there is k₁ with 1/2 ≤ c_k ≤ 2 for k ≥ k₁. For such k, f_k and f_∞ vanish outside the compact ball K := B̄_{2R}(y). Moreover ‖f_k − f_∞‖_∞ → 0. Outside K both functions vanish. On K, |(w − y)/c_k − (w − y)| ≤ 2R|c_k⁻¹ − 1| → 0, and f is uniformly continuous.
4. Uniform bound (Banach–Steinhaus). Let X_K be the space of bounded continuous h : ℝ^P → ℝ with h = 0 outside K, with the sup norm. It is a closed subspace of the Banach space of bounded continuous functions, hence complete. For each k, Λ_k(h) := ∫ h g_k dμ is a linear map X_K → ℝ^Q with |Λ_k(h)| ≤ ‖h‖_∞ ∫_K |g_k| dμ < ∞, because g_k is locally integrable and K is compact. So Λ_k is a bounded operator. Every h ∈ X_K is continuous with compact support (spt h ⊆ K), so (Λ_k h)_k converges by hypothesis and is bounded. By the uniform boundedness principle (Mathlib banach_steinhaus) there is M < ∞ with ‖Λ_k‖ ≤ M for all k.
5. For k ≥ k₁, f_k − f_∞ ∈ X_K, and both f_k g_k and f_∞ g_k are integrable. So |∫ f_k g_k dμ − ∫ f_∞ g_k dμ| = |Λ_k(f_k − f_∞)| ≤ M‖f_k − f_∞‖_∞ → 0 by step 3.
6. f_∞ is continuous with compact support, so ∫ f_∞ g_k dμ → ∫ f_∞ g dμ by hypothesis. With step 5, ∫ f_k g_k dμ → ∫ f_∞ g dμ. Since c_k^{−n} → 1, step 2 gives ∫ f(x) g_k(y + c_k x) dμ(x) = c_k^{−n}∫ f_k g_k dμ → ∫ f_∞ g dμ = ∫ f(x) g(y + x) dμ(x). ∎
proof_key_steps: affine change of variables: ∫h(y+cx)dμH[n] = c^{-n}∫h dμH[n] for every h
the rescaled test functions f((w−y)/c_k) converge uniformly to f(w−y), with supports in a fixed compact K
Banach–Steinhaus on the complete space of bounded continuous functions vanishing off K bounds h ↦ ∫h g_k uniformly in k
combine with weak convergence tested against the fixed function f(·−y), and with c_k^{-n} → 1

audit.reason: The exact contract permits arbitrary g, as does the proof: affine change of variables remains valid for totalized Bochner integrals. Local integrability of each g_k supplies bounded operators on the complete fixed-support test-function space; Banach–Steinhaus and uniform convergence of the moving tests establish the claimed limit without an unstated local-finiteness assumption.
